Class ForwardedHeaders

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.http.server.util.ForwardedHeaders
public final class ForwardedHeaders extends Object
Writes the forwarding headers of a request relayed to an upstream server: X-Forwarded-For, X-Forwarded-Proto, X-Forwarded-Host, X-Forwarded-Port, X-Forwarded-Prefix and the RFC 7239 Forwarded header.

Whether the forwarding headers that the inbound request already carries are kept depends on whether the peer that sent it is a trusted proxy:

  • From a trusted proxy, this hop is appended to X-Forwarded-For and Forwarded, and the X-Forwarded-Proto, -Host, -Port and -Prefix values the first proxy set are kept. If the trusted chain only comes in one of the two formats, it is translated to the other one before this hop is appended (RFC 7239 section 7.4), so that both headers describe the same chain: a downstream server that prefers Forwarded must not see this hop as the client.
  • From any other peer, the inbound values could be forged, so they are replaced with the values of this hop.
By default no peer is trusted.

The trust predicate only evaluates the immediate peer, i.e. the remote address of the connection the inbound request arrived on. The addresses inside the inbound headers are never tested. With a chain of proxies in front of this server, e.g. two, trust the nearer one, and rely on it having applied the same rule to its own peer.
